title: Unit – 4 : Session – 5 : SLO – 1  |  Implementation of Tree Using Array — Concepts
sections: The array representation of binary tree can be done using a technique called SEQUENTIAL (LEVEL-ORDER) REPRESENTATION.
In level-order traversal, the elements of the binary tree are stored in the array in the order in which they are visited in a BREADTH-FIRST (LEVEL-ORDER) TRAVERSAL.
The array representation of binary tree allows for efficient RANDOM ACCESS to the elements of the tree.
If a binary tree has n nodes, the array representation of the tree can be stored in an array of size n, allowing for DIRECT (O(1)) access to each node in the tree.
The ROOT of the binary tree is stored at the first position of the array.
The left child of node i can be found at position 2*i.
The right child of node i can be found at position 2*i + 1.
The parent of node i can be found at position floor(i/2).
The array representation of binary tree can be useful in algorithms that require fast access to the elements of a tree, such as HEAP SORT or PRIORITY QUEUE (searching) algorithms.
It is important to note that not all binary trees can be EFFICIENTLY represented in an array, as the SIZE (number of nodes) in the array must be known in advance.
